text:
tara: quick sync — sketching a cross-lang surface for paginated APIs. thinking of explicit PullCursor vs PushStream split so SDKs can pick ergonomic defaults.

sam: can you sketch the tradeoffs? curious about transport choices (grpc/http2/ws) + how retries work across both modes.

tara: high level:
- PullCursor: client asks for pages, gets opaque resume token. easy for RPCs that are idempotent per-page. works with unary http2/grpc.
- PushStream: server streams items and can signal backpressure. best for websockets/http2/server-stream. nicer for TS ReadableStream and Go channels.

diego: +1. retries are the tricky bit. proposal: per-request idempotency metadata + per-page resume token. semantics:
- PullCursor: server returns (items, resume_token, page_id, idempotency_key_optional)
- on transient error client retries using last resume_token; server must treat resume_token as authoritative for continuity.

sam: runtime ergonomics ideas (TS/Python/Go):

TS example (PushStream default for streaming endpoints):
```
// returns AsyncIterable<Item>
const stream = client.listAllFilesStream(query)
for await (const item of stream) { /*...*/ }
```

TS PullCursor variant:
```
const cursor = await client.listFilesCursor(q)
let page
while ((page = await cursor.next()) !== null) { page.items.forEach(...) }
```

Python sketch:
```
# async iterator is the default for streaming
async for item in client.list_files_stream(q):
    ...
# cursor
cursor = client.list_files_cursor(q)
page = cursor.next()  # sync or awaitable depending on transport
```

Go sketch:
```
// channel-style for push
ch := client.ListFilesStream(ctx, q)
for item := range ch { ... }
// pull
cursor := client.ListFilesCursor(ctx, q)
for cursor.Next() { page := cursor.Page() ... }
```

diego: for transport: grpc streaming maps naturally to PushStream; http/1.1 long poll -> PullCursor. websockets can do push but we need a pressure signal: prefer to surface a small flow-control callback in SDKs rather than raw bytes.

tara: edge cases:
- if client uses PushStream but network blips, we fallback to resuming via PullCursor using latest resume_token (server must provide it periodically).
- auth/route changes: resume_token must be short-lived and rebindable with same permissions.

sam: testing + rollout: we should add an interop harness that runs against a mock server supporting both modes and asserts resume semantics + retry counters. also record latency impact of prefetching pages in PullCursor.

ci-bot: design doc draft created: https://rwd.internal/docs/pull-vs-push-paginator-draft (test harness job queued) :white_check_mark:

tara: next steps: I'll update the RFC with API sketches above, add a compatibility matrix for transports, and a minimal shim that maps PushStream -> PullCursor for legacy endpoints. ping @sam @diego for review by EOD tomorrow :eyes:
